dedupe_keys.name: empirical validation of building energy simulation in lbnl s flexlab testbed 2019 to 2022

description: FLEXLAB at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory is a testbed where building and grid technologies are developed and tested singly or as integrated systems under real-world conditions, monitoring everything from plug loads to envelopes and controls, and now extended with FLEXGRID for building-to-grid research. In the DOE project Empirical Validation of Energy Simulation: FLEXLAB (October 2019 to September 2022, budget $1.95 million, with Argonne National Laboratory), researchers instrumented FLEXLAB cells to produce detailed validation datasets for energy simulation, following a first phase on heating and cooling loads in empty rooms with mixing ventilation. The second phase studied thermal loads with furniture, different internal gains and varied air flow rates for overhead mixing ventilation and radiant slab and panel systems, with the aim of documenting measured datasets, adding them to ASHRAE Standard 140 and helping the EnergyPlus team correct deficiencies. Coverage: test cells at Berkeley Lab, California. Access: project descriptions and publications; FLEXLAB testing by arrangement. Licence: U.S. government information. Caveats: the datasets themselves were not located on the pages read, and test cells represent commercial perimeter zones only. Simulation uses are validating and calibrating building energy simulation engines. Related records: the ASHRAE Standard 140 BESTEST resource files and the NIST Net-Zero Energy Residential Test Facility.
